correctness.rationale: For R=k[[t^2,t^3]], a proper finite-colength ideal of least valuation d contains t^{d+2}k[[t]] because multiplication by its unit-normalized least-valuation element carries the conductor t^2k[[t]] into I. This yields the full P^1 colength-n family for each n>=2 (and unique ideals at n=0,1). Modulo x=t^2, colengths 2,3 each have an A^1 contact-one stratum and one contact-two boundary; n>=4 has only contact two and class 1+L. Their exact motivic sum is the claimed G. The general x^u-germ substitution is explicitly a stated premise, Huang--Jiang--Oblomkov Corollary 6.8, not derived from finite experiments. The n=0 and u=0 cases and G(Q,1)=(1+L Q^2)/(1-Q) match. Independent symbolic specialization verified; check of the general substitution is conditional on the cited primary theorem, whose complete text was inaccessible during this run.
